title: Most news apps treat personalization like a blunt instrument.
body:
They assume that because you clicked on one article about electric vehicles, you want a feed flooded with every single EV press release ever written. That is not how human curiosity works. We are nuanced creatures. We read about technology because we care about the future, but we also read about local politics because we care about our neighborhoods. We read about global markets, but we also enjoy a longform profile on a niche hobby.

At Headlinne, we built our recommendation engine to respect that complexity. It does not just track what you click. It looks at the signal in the noise. It learns which topics you follow for professional growth versus which ones you follow for pure interest. It understands that reading a headline is different from reading an entire piece.

The goal is not to trap you in a bubble of things you already know. The goal is to surface the stories that actually add value to your day. When the algorithm stops guessing and starts learning your actual patterns, the news stops feeling like a chore and starts feeling like a conversation.
cta: See how we are rethinking the way you get your news at HEADLINNE.com.
